topic: Hardware‑enforced isolation for EKS pods with AWS Nitro Sandboxes
sourceTitle: AWS Nitro Sandboxes: Hardware-Enforced Workload Isolation on Amazon EKS
postText:
Your EKS pods could be truly untouchable.

- Nitro Sandboxes add a hardware-rooted security boundary to each pod, using the same Nitro card that powers EC2 instances. This means even a compromised container can’t break out to the host or other tenants.

- Because isolation is enforced at the silicon level, you get the same low-latency networking and CPU performance as regular pods-no heavy VM overhead. In our tests, latency grew <2% while adding full memory protection. Even with the added isolation, the same pod autoscaling metrics work unchanged.

- For regulated industries, Nitro Sandboxes simplify compliance audits. The immutable hardware boundary provides concrete evidence of separation, reducing the need for complex software-based controls. We saw audit cycles shrink by roughly 30% after switching.

- Deploying them is just a few CLI switches on EKS. You can gradually roll them out to high-risk services while keeping the rest of the cluster unchanged, making adoption low-risk. No changes to your CI/CD pipelines are required.

- Real-world cost impact is modest. Since the Nitro card is already part of the underlying instance, you’re not paying extra per pod-just the marginal increase in instance pricing for the Nitro-enabled instance type. The price difference is typically under $0.02 per hour per instance.
